newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: News Corp trying to sell PMP stake - paper.
newsitem.headline: News Corp trying to sell PMP stake - paper.

text.p: News Corp Ltd is trying to sell its 40 percent stake in multi-media group PMP Communiciations Ltd for A$3.20 a share through Were Stockbroking, The Australian and The Sydney Morning Herald newspapers reported on Wednesday.
"The Australian understands fund managers have been approached by JB Were to buy PMP shares at about A$3.20 each -- a 12 percent discount to yesterday's closing price of A$3.65," The Australian said.
"Overseas buyers have also been sounded out by Were to gauge demand for the scrip," The Australian said.

"Despite the steep discount in the price there was no formal announcement from News Corp last night, triggering speculation that Were had struggled to find enough institutional interest to find a home for all of its shares," The Sydney Morning Herald newspaper said.
"News had hoped to get a higher price for its controlling stake by eliciting a takeover bid from an international player," the Herald said.
"It is believed U.S. based R.R. Donnelly & Sons expressed interest in PMP, but baulked at News' asking price of A$3.80 to A$4.00 a share," it said.
Donnelley & Sons already has a 2.2 percent stake in PMP and vice chairman James Donnelley is already a director.
Spokesmen for News Corp and PMP were not immediately available for comment.
